chapter: Hollywood life and the musicians' union
title: The Musicians Credit Union and Local 802
summary: Carter denies much credit for the credit union Milt Hinton says he founded.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Very good. Now, two more things. The brief one first. In the Time Life records recreation of the Swing Era, in a book they published, Milt Hinton is quoted as saying that "People don't know this, but Benny -- referring to you -- is responsible for the Musicians Credit Union. It's very hard for musicians to get loans, because they have nothing to give a bank as collateral. Benny confidently went to Local 802 and got them to set up a credit union, and he put in the first $18,000. That was 5 or 6 years ago -- and it's still going strong." Five or six years ago would have been, then, in about the mid 1960's. I'm not sure that this doesn't really relate to Hollywood very much perhaps, but he's talking about Local 802 which is in New York, isn't it?
You're still a member of that.
Oh yes, that was my first local, yes.
So what was that all about.

Oh, I don't know. I can't take any credit for setting up the credit union. I think ... well, I just made a deposit, you know, in the credit union, and I think I was maybe the first depositor, or something; I don't know. And that's all, you know.
All the exaggerations in our discussion are exaggerations that other people make of your role which you then reduce. You never increased the role that you played in anything.
Well, that's the way it is.
